name: notify-home-assistant
description: Send a phone notification through the Home Assistant companion app. INPUT (the same for every notify-* adapter): the node before this one returns `notification: {title?, body, priority?: low|normal|high, tag?, link?, actions?: [{title, link, one_tap?}]}`; `skip: true` sends nothing. Links must be https; anything else is not sent and is counted. At most 3 actions. OUTPUT (the same for every adapter): {provider, sent, skipped, dry_run, status, actions_sent, actions_dropped, one_tap_actions, link_sent, link_dropped, tag_sent}. To change service, swap this module on the send node (swap_node_module) and set the other adapter's config; nothing upstream changes. See docs/notification-contract.md. WHAT HOME ASSISTANT DOES WITH IT: high priority is sent as priority high with ttl 0; `link` is what a tap opens; every action OPENS its link (one_tap is not available through this service without an automation inside Home Assistant, so one_tap_actions is 0 and a Talos action link shows its confirmation page); `tag` is sent, so a later message with the same tag replaces the earlier one. REPLY BOX (this adapter only, not part of the notification): with REPLY_TITLE set, every notification this node sends also carries a reply action and the phone shows a text field under it; what is typed is NOT returned to this module — the companion app fires `mobile_app_notification_action` (action REPLY, with `reply_text`) inside Home Assistant, where an automation of yours decides what happens to it. The box takes one of the three action places, so with three composed actions the last is not sent and is counted in actions_dropped. Written from the companion app's documented format; a plain notification and a tag were delivered through a live server on 2026-10-04, the reply box on 2026-10-09. A response that is not 2xx fails the node with the host and the status, never the body. BASE_URL must be an https:// address the worker can reach: a home-network address (192.168.x.x, homeassistant.local) is refused by the worker; use the external address. GRANTS: installs with NO allowed hosts and no secrets, so it can reach nothing until you say what it may reach: set the server's host with update_module_hosts and the token's exact path with update_module_secrets. Use one installed copy per server. CREDENTIALS: the module never holds one; AUTH_HEADER carries a vault:// reference the host replaces when the request is sent.

NOTIFY_SERVICE.description: The notify service for the phone, without the 'notify.' prefix: for example mobile_app_<device>.

AUTH_HEADER.description: 'Bearer vault://homeassistant/token' — a long-lived access token from your Home Assistant profile, stored in the vault.

DRY_RUN.description: true: check the notification and the config, send nothing, and report what would be sent.

REPLY_TITLE.description: Optional. The label of a reply box added under every notification this node sends, for example 'Add to list'. Unset or blank: no box. What is typed is handled by an automation inside Home Assistant (event mobile_app_notification_action, action REPLY, reply_text), not by this module.

setup_instructions.title: Find the notify service
setup_instructions.detail: In Home Assistant, Developer tools > Actions lists notify.mobile_app_<device> once the companion app is signed in.

setup_instructions.title: Store a token
setup_instructions.detail: Create a long-lived access token in your Home Assistant profile and store it in the vault under homeassistant/token. Tokens are not stored through MCP.

setup_instructions.title: Grant the installed copy
setup_instructions.detail: update_module_hosts with Home Assistant's external host; update_module_secrets with homeassistant/token.

setup_instructions.title: Rehearse
setup_instructions.detail: Set DRY_RUN true and read the result: it reports what would be sent, and sends nothing.
